problem: The column header says the columns are σx, σy, τxy, but the θ=45° row actually holds σx′, σy′ and τx′y′, and the invariant row holds the sums σx+σy and σx′+σy′, not components. A student can read 120 MPa as a normal stress on the x-face.
fix: Label the columns by face/direction (normal stress on x-face, normal stress on y-face, shear on x-face), or state in the caption that row 2 shows the transformed components σx′, σy′, τx′y′ and row 3 shows the two sums σx+σy and σx′+σy′.

problem: "At θ = 45° the normal stresses stay 100 MPa and 20 MPa" is true only for these particular numbers (τxy = 40 MPa exactly offsets the (σx−σy)/2 cos 2θ term, which is zero at 45°). Read alone, it suggests normal stresses never change at 45°, which contradicts the general equations and Q3.
fix: Say: "For this state (σx = 100 MPa, σy = 20 MPa, τxy = 40 MPa) the normal stresses at θ = 45° happen to come back as 100 MPa and 20 MPa, while the shear changes from +40 MPa to −40 MPa; the sum stays 120 MPa in every orientation."
